title: WPMS/2800/2013 of Rishipal Chauhan Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 2800 of 2013 (M/S)
Rishipal Chauhan .....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .....Respondents
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl. C.S.C. for the State.
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Counter affidavit alongwith delay condonation
application as well as supplementary counter affidavit is
handed over in the Court which is taken on record.
For the reasons stated in the application, delay in
filing counter affidavit is condoned. Counter affidavit is
taken on record.
Coordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated
11.09.2013, in Writ Petition No. 2206 of 2013, has
passed order as under:-
"This petition has been filed by the petitioner
for quashing the impugned order/letter dated
23.08.2013 passed/ issued by the respondent no.3
to respondent no.2, by which he has referred the
resolution dated 30.06.2013 of Gram Panchayat
Rudrapur, Block and Tehsil Vikas Nagar, district
Dehradun appointing the respondent no.5 as Fair
Price Shopkeeper. Further prayer has been made
for a direction to the respondent nos.1 to 4 to
appoint the petitioner as Fair Price Shopkeeper of
Gram Panchayat Rudrapur, Block and Tehsil Vikas
Nagar, district Dehradun.
The ground taken in the writ petition is that
the recommendation in favour of respondent no.5
has been made in violation of Government Order
dated 11.07.2011, which provides the eligibility of
the candidates for Fair Price Shop. This
Government Order provides that only such
persons shall be eligible for Fair Price Shop, whose

2
economic condition is good and is in a position to
lift the ration of one month. This Government
Order further provides that the candidate should
have good reputation and he should be literate so
that he could maintain the accounts of shop
properly.
The contention of the learned counsel for the
petitioner is that the respondent no.5 belongs to
B.P.L. category and his annual income is less than
Rs. 15,000/- and therefore, he is not covered
under the relevant Government Order. Learned
counsel for the petitioner contended that since the
respondent no.5 is not eligible for allotment of Fair
Price Shop under the relevant Government Order,
the concerned Fair Price Shop cannot be allotted in
his favour. Learned counsel for the petitioner
further submitted that the petitioner has made a
representation in this regard before the District
Supply Officer, Dehradun on 29.08.2013, but the
same has not been decided so far.
Learned Addl. C.S.C. for the State, on the
other hand, submitted that the petitioner has not
enclosed any documentary evidence in support of
his submission and has only made such
submission in the body of the writ petition.
Considering the submission advanced by the
learned counsel for the parties, the writ petition is
disposed of with a direction to the District Supply
Officer, Dehradun to consider and take final
decision on the representation of the petitioner
dated 29.08.2013, if not taken earlier,
expeditiously, preferably within a period of one
month from the date of production of a certified
copy of this order. The District Supply Officer,
Dehradun, before taking final decision on the
representation of the petitioner, shall hear the
respondent no.5 also."
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, learned counsel appearing
for the petitioner, submits that instead of taking final
decision on the representation of the petitioner dated
29.08.2013 as directed by this Court vide order dated
11.09.2013, District Supply Officer has passed order on

3
27th November, 2013, annexure No.1 to the
supplementary counter affidavit, filed by the
respondents.
Perusal of the order dated 27.11.2013 reveals that
District Supply Officer has appointed respondent No.5
Sohan Singh as licencee of fair price shop pursuant to
the direction / approval issued by the District Collector,
Dehradun.
Perusal of the recommendation made by the
District Supply Officer dated 01.11.2013, page 6 to the
supplementary counter affidavit, would reveal that
District Supply Officer has observed that earlier
respondent No. 5 was B.P.L. card holder, however,
thereafter, he acquired the status of A.P.L., therefore, he
was found suitable to run the fair price shop. There is
absolutely no discussion in the recommendation dated
01.11.2013 made by the District Supply officer as to
when respondent No. 5 has acquired the status of A.P.L.
nor it is stated that respondent No. 5 has financial
capacity to pay for ration of one month in advance nor it
is found as to whether respondent No.5 is literate so that
he can maintain the account. There is no discussion
about the reputation of respondent No. 5 which are sine
quo non to issue him fair price shop in accordance with
the Government Order. Impugned order and
recommendation are totally silent about the
qualification / dis-qualification of the petitioner.
Learned Standing Counsel submits that decision
shall be taken afresh in the present matter after hearing
the petitioner as well as respondent No.5 within six

4
weeks from today and both the parties shall be given
liberty to place on record evidence to prove and dis-prove the claims and counter claims.
In view of the above, present writ petition is
allowed. Impugned order dated 27.11.2013 is directed to
be kept in abeyance. Respondent No.2 is directed to
take decision afresh preferably within six weeks from
today after hearing petitioner as well as respondent
No.5 and after giving opportunity to respondent No.5
and petitioner to place on record their respective
evidence to prove and dis-prove claims and counter
claims. While taking the decision, respondent No. 2
shall pass reasoned and speaking order.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
Dated 11th April, 2014 Shiv
